ai.description: This frog reaches 4–6 cm. It features a brown or olive dorsum with a distinct golden-yellow dorsolateral fold and a white upper lip. Long, slender limbs and fully webbed toes are characteristic.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hylarana montana* is best distinguished by its distinct, unbroken light dorsolateral folds that extend clearly from the snout to the groin, unlike many similar regional species.
ai.habitat: The Mountain Golden-backed Frog inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at elevations above 800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Mountain Golden-backed Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects along the banks of fast-flowing mountain streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana montana* breeds during the monsoon season, laying large clutches of pigmented eggs in stagnant forest pools or slow-moving streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Mountain Golden-backed Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, typically found in high-elevation evergreen forests above 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Mountain Golden-backed Frog produces a series of rapid, high-pitched "ticking" notes, typically heard near fast-flowing streams in montane forests.
